blockTypes.circuit: Exercises performed sequentially as a circuit.
blockTypes.warmup: Low-intensity preparation before the main work.

weeks.title: Movement Foundation
weeks.focus: Learn movement patterns, establish baseline mobility and build basic strength.

blocks.name: Warm-up
blocks.instructions: Move continuously at low intensity. Do not force range of motion.

blocks.name: Lower Body Strength
blocks.instructions: Rest 60–90 sec between sets. Use a load that leaves approximately 2–3 good reps in reserve.

blocks.name: Post-Workout Mobility
blocks.instructions: Stretch gently. No bouncing and no sharp pain.

blocks.name: Court Movement
blocks.instructions: Keep intensity moderate. Prioritize footwork quality over speed.

blocks.name: Badminton Play
blocks.instructions: Play normally. Avoid maximum-intensity lunges during the first week.

blocks.name: Upper Body Strength
blocks.instructions: Controlled repetitions. Avoid training to failure.

blocks.name: 10 Minute Mobility
blocks.instructions: This should feel restorative, not like a workout.

blocks.name: Full Body
blocks.instructions: Moderate intensity. Leave 2–3 reps in reserve.

blocks.name: Badminton Session
blocks.instructions: Play at moderate intensity. Focus on footwork and efficient recovery.

weeks.title: Movement Foundation Progression
weeks.focus: Increase volume slightly while maintaining movement quality.

progression.strength: Add 1–2 reps where technically possible before increasing weight.

blocks.name: Lower Body Strength
blocks.instructions: Same exercises as Week 1. Increase load slightly only if all repetitions are clean.

weeks.title: Range and Control
weeks.focus: Build strength through progressively larger ranges of motion.

progression.strength: Increase load 2.5–5% if all Week 2 repetitions were comfortable.
progression.mobility: Increase range rather than forcing longer holds.

blocks.name: Lower Body Strength
blocks.instructions: Use full comfortable range of motion.

weeks.title: Foundation Consolidation
weeks.focus: Consolidate movement quality and prepare for heavier strength work.

progression.strength: Maintain volume and increase load slightly if technique is excellent.

weeks.title: Strength Through Range
weeks.focus: Begin heavier strength work while maintaining mobility.

progression.strength: Use challenging loads with 2 reps in reserve.

blocks.name: Power Introduction
blocks.instructions: Maximum quality, not maximum fatigue. Stop if landing mechanics deteriorate.

weeks.title: Active Flexibility
weeks.focus: Develop active control at longer muscle lengths.

progression.power: Keep jumps low volume and high quality.

weeks.title: Strength and Lateral Range
weeks.focus: Improve lateral strength and badminton-specific range.

progression.strength: Increase load while maintaining full range.
progression.mobility: Use deeper Cossack and lateral lunge positions.

weeks.title: End-Range Strength
weeks.focus: Make the new mobility strong and repeatable.

weeks.title: Explosive Movement
weeks.focus: Convert strength and mobility into faster badminton movement.

progression.strength: Keep heavy work at moderate volume.

blocks.name: High-Quality Footwork
blocks.instructions: Move fast but remain technically controlled.

blocks.name: Power
blocks.instructions: Rest 60–90 sec between sets. Every repetition should be explosive.

weeks.title: Acceleration and Deceleration
weeks.focus: Improve the ability to accelerate into and safely recover from lunges.

weeks.title: Badminton-Specific Athleticism
weeks.focus: Combine mobility, strength, acceleration and court movement.

weeks.title: Performance and Assessment
weeks.focus: Consolidate the program and assess improvements in mobility, strength and court movement.

blocks.name: Court Movement Assessment
blocks.instructions: Compare movement quality and fatigue against Week 1.

blocks.name: Mobility Assessment
blocks.instructions: Compare your range and control against Week 1.

blocks.name: Explosive Movement
blocks.instructions: This is a quality session, not a conditioning test.

blocks.name: Badminton
blocks.instructions: Play normally and assess whether deep lunges, recovery and lateral movement feel easier than Week 1.
